new_statements.quote: Duração das vogais. Na penúltima sílaba, geralmente a sílaba tónica, ocorre um ligeiro alongamento da vogal que, na escrita, não será assinalado. (1) apana 'não está', baba 'pai'. [...] [p.174] Tom. Reconhece-se a existência de tonalidade em algumas palavras de Ciwute. Contudo, a relevância do tom nesta língua não se afigura bastante para se impor a sua marcação na escrita.
new_statements.translation: Vowel length. On the penultimate syllable, generally the stressed (tonic) syllable, there is a slight lengthening of the vowel, which will not be marked in writing. (1) apana 'is not (here)', baba 'father'. [...] Tone. The existence of tonality in some words of Ciwute is recognised. However, the relevance of tone in this language does not appear sufficient to require marking it in writing.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress (with slight vowel lengthening) falls on the penultimate syllable; the language also has some lexical tone, which the orthography leaves unmarked.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the hedge 'geralmente' (generally); no exceptions listed.
new_statements.domain_note: Stated for words in isolation (orthography report, citation-form examples apana, baba); Gowlett 2003 describes the Zone-S penultimate length-stress as phrase-final in declaratives, so the word-level statement may reflect citation forms = one-word phrases. Reference variety: Ciwute of Chimoio city and surroundings.
new_statements.identity_note: The 2011 chapter describes 'Ciwute' (authors' spelling; speakers say Ciutee/Chiwutee), Guthrie S13b, reference variety = the speech of Chimoio city and surroundings, Manica province — this is Glottolog tewe1238 / ISO twx. Doke 1931 and Wikipedia treat Teve/Tewe as a sub-dialect of Manyika (many1258); the statement quoted is Tewe-specific, not a Manyika or general-Shona statement.
